rules.sentence: Only spontaneous cases presenting with weakness of the muscles innervated by the anterior interosseous nerve qualify as true anterior interosseous nerve syndrome.
Injuries to the anterior interosseous nerve resulting from direct external trauma do not meet the diagnostic criteria for anterior interosseous nerve syndrome.[6]
Most cases resolve spontaneously, and conservative management, including symptomatic treatment over a period of 3 to 6 months, remains the preferred initial strategy.[3]
